{{Top|canon=Sith king|notoc=1}}
{{Quote|The guardian beasts called tuk'ata stand watch over the tombs and protect them from desecration. They have long been the royal companions of Sith Kings.|Extract from ''[[Jen'jidai]]'' [[Sorzus Syn]]'s [[Sorzus Syn's chronicle|titular chronicle]]|<ref name="BoS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
"'''Sith King'''" was a title traditionally held by certain rulers of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith species]] prior to the arrival of the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Exiles]] to [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] at the end of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]]<ref name="BoS" /> in [[6900 BBY]].<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

Due to the kratocratic cultural mores of the Sith people,<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Sith Kings were generally among the most powerful [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force users]] of their [[Time/Legends|times]] and often engaged in protracted campaigns of conquest against their rivals.<ref name="K:PoLS3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031016korriban3|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 3: The Dark Lord's Heart}}</ref> Many Sith Kings were protected by [[Tuk'ata/Legends|tuk'ata]] [[Sithspawn/Legends|Sithspawn]] companions in life and death, buried in such sacred locations as the [[Valley of the Dark Lords/Legends|Valley of the Sleeping Kings]]<ref name="BoS" /> and the [[Valley of Golg]].<ref name="K:PoLS3" />

Among the most notable Sith Kings were [[Adas]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref><ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> [[Dathka Graush/Legends|Dathka Graush]],<ref name="LSatSoM">''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]''</ref> and [[Hakagram Graush]], the latter of whom was the last to have held the title prior to the formal establishment of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] by the Exiles.<ref name="BoS" /> The title fell out of widespread usage in the years that followed, replaced by the equivalent title ''[[Jen'ari]]'' meaning "[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]" in the [[Sith (language)|Sith language]].<ref name="END" /><ref name="TCSWEII154">{{CSWECite|II|154|''Jen'ari''}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Though Sith holding the title of "King" have appeared in the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity since Adas was introduced in [[1996]]'s ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'', the term "Sith King" was first employed as a fully capitalized title on page 118 of the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' and on page 142 of the [[2010]] sourcebook ''[[The Unknown Regions]]''. It first saw usage as a proper noun in its own right on page 37 of the [[2012]] reference book ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''.

''[[Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls]]'', which was published when<ref name="K:PoLS">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031002korriban|text=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|int=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls}}</ref> the [[canon]] was that the first [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] reigned ~[[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]],<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> refers to Dathka Graush as a "Dark Lord" who reigned "over seven millennia before the Battle of Yavin."<ref name="K:PoLS3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20031016korriban3|series=Korriban: Planet of Lost Souls|text=Part 3: The Dark Lord's Heart}}</ref> However, ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the first Dark Lord of the Sith to have reigned in [[6900 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> a century after Graush's reign.<ref name="K:PoLS3" /> ''[[Luke Skywalker and the Shadows of Mindor]]'' retconned Dathka Graush to be a "King of the Sith".<ref name="LSatSoM" />
